articles.headline: Trump departs for Asia trip focusing on trade deals and nuclear talks
articles.title: Trump’s Asia trip: Deals in Manila and Shenzhen, nuclear summit with Xi and Putin, maybe Kim meeting
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump departed for Asia on November 16, 2026, to pursue economic agreements and three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning called the trilateral meeting groundbreaking. The visit follows domestic political setbacks for Trump, including Republican losses in the midterm congressional elections.
articles.description: Trump said he plans to talk about Russia's war in Ukraine during the highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin in China

articles.headline: Seventeen people killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa
articles.title: At least 17 killed in two South Africa mass shootings
articles.summary: At least seventeen people were killed in two separate mass shootings across South Africa on November 16, 2026, according to police. National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola stated that investigators have not yet established motives for the attacks occurring 530 kilometres apart in Sweetwaters and Jeffsville. Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni noted potential links to a previous mass shooting.
articles.description: Eight men killed in shooting near Pietermaritzburg while six men and three women shot dead near Pretoria.

articles.headline: Estonia closes Russian border crossings following drone factory arson attempt
articles.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
articles.summary: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal announced that border crossings with Russia will close on December 1 following an attempted arson attack at a drone manufacturing facility north of Tallinn. The facility, operated by Threod Systems, was targeted by suspects local media reported to be Latvian. Moscow dismissed the accusations as baseless while European leaders continue to express concern over alleged Russian hybrid warfare.
articles.description: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.

articles.headline: Nine-month-old baby dies from hypothermia in Khan Younis displacement camp
articles.title: ‘My arms are empty’: Tragedy strikes Gaza family after baby dies from cold
articles.summary: Kinan Arqiq, a nine-month-old infant living in a makeshift camp in southern Gaza, died on November 12 from a severe drop in body temperature. Medical sources confirmed the fatality, marking the first cold-related death of the current winter season. The infant's parents, Susan and Ahmed Arqiq, stated they lacked adequate shelter and blankets due to ongoing border blockades restricting essential materials from entering the Palestinian territory.
articles.description: A nine-month-old baby has died from hypothermia inside his family’s displacement tent in Gaza, as winter returns.

articles.headline: Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandeb as Houthi troops advance
articles.title: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces pull out of Bab al-Mandeb
articles.summary: Forces aligned with the internationally recognised Yemeni government withdrew from Dhubab airport and territory near the Bab al-Mandeb strait on Sunday to defend Aden. Military experts noted that the retreat risks cutting off coastal supply routes and leaves a strategic vacuum filled by Houthi forces. The conflict escalated as government-aligned forces increased airstrikes while Houthi fighters responded with ballistic missiles and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia.
articles.description: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces retreat from the Red Sea coast, threatening global maritime security.

articles.headline: Imran Khan appeals to Pakistan top judges for urgent medical care
articles.title: Jailed Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan writes to judges, seeks vital medical care
articles.summary: Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan released an open letter on Monday through his lawyer Salman Safdar, appealing to Pakistan’s Supreme Court for urgent medical treatment for himself and his wife, Bushra Bibi. Khan, 74, stated he has been held in solitary confinement and suffers from failing vision and high health risks. His legal team requested judicial intervention to enforce prior medical orders and ensure proper hospital care.
articles.description: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party founder says court orders on his care were ignored and he ‘may not return alive’.

articles.headline: Russian attacks kill three in Ukraine as European Union criticises Moscow
articles.title: Russian attacks kill three in Ukraine, EU accuses Moscow of prolonging war
articles.summary: Russian military strikes killed three individuals across the Kherson, Dnipropetrovsk, and Zaporizhia regions of Ukraine on Monday. Concurrently, European Union High Representative Kaja Kallas accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of utilizing maximalist demands to prolong the conflict. In response to mounting infrastructure damage, the European Commission disbursed 1.88 billion dollars for defense systems alongside a separate 8.7 billion euro payment to support Ukraine.
articles.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says Russian President Vladimir Putin is making maximalist demands.

articles.headline: COP31 talks face sluggish climate finance responses amid Western security pressures
articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.summary: Urgent demands for climate finance from vulnerable developing nations met a slow response at the COP31 summit in Antalya as Western governments prioritized national security and domestic living costs. Host country Turkiye and Australia focused on implementing existing pledges rather than setting new targets. While multilateral development banks reported record lending in 2025, analysts noted significant funding gaps driven by geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal spaces, and high capital costs.
articles.description: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

articles.headline: Nvidia faces uncertainty following resignation of CEO Jensen Huang
articles.title: The Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing down
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following a scandal involving multiple affairs and allegations of chip smuggling to China. CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim leader while the company faces investigations and a 14 percent stock drop. Analysts suggest the long-term impact on the AI industry remains unclear despite the leadership transition.
articles.description: For years, Jensen Huang has had an almost unprecedented power to shape AI's advancement as Nvidia's CEO, cofounder, and president. As The Verge wrote last week, Nvidia's chips are "the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built." Ever-increasing demand has consistently outpaced supply, leading AI CEOs to essentially bow at […]

articles.headline: Wholesale prices rise 12.29% year-on-year in October across India
articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.summary: Government data released on November 16, 2026, showed that wholesale inflation quickened to 12.29% year-on-year in October, surpassing the previous month's rate of 11.39% and economists' average forecast of 12.1%. The increase was driven by higher prices across sectors, with fuel and power recording a sharp surge of 32.84% compared to the previous year.
articles.description: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders stricter monitoring of pollution in Yamuna river
articles.title: Pollution in Yamuna increased despite huge expenditure on cleaning: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has directed the Central Pollution Control Board to monitor water quality at state and district borders, citing rising pollution despite significant cleanup spending. The court emphasized that industrial and sewage waste must be treated at the source and warned that authorities will face penalties if water quality deteriorates under their jurisdiction.
articles.description: “This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna,” said SC

articles.headline: Beijing hails upcoming US, China and Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.title: Beijing hails ‘groundbreaking significance’ of U.S., China, Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.summary: China announced that President Xi Jinping will host U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, during the APEC gathering. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning praised the historic trilateral meeting as having groundbreaking significance. Experts note the talks will likely focus on Ukraine and energy supplies despite existing geopolitical tensions.
articles.description: The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control

articles.headline: European Union accuses Russia of stalling peace talks and targeting infrastructure
articles.title: EU accuses Russia of stalling Ukraine peace talks to target power plants as winter nears
articles.summary: European Union foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on November 16, 2026, criticized Russia for escalating the nearly five-year war by attacking civilian infrastructure as winter approaches. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas dismissed U.S.-encouraged Russian demands for a new European security framework as absurd, noting that Russia initiated the conflict. Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee announced upcoming sanctions targeting financial mechanisms supporting the war.
articles.description: At talks in Brussels, EU foreign ministers said the priority should be to secure a ceasefire and then a real peace agreement

articles.headline: French soldiers operate in Ukraine on secret mission since summer
articles.title: French troops deployed in Ukraine on secret mission: RFI
articles.summary: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months on a confidential mission codenamed Volia, Radio France Internationale reported on November 16, 2026. The light structure, led by a French general, trains Ukrainian troops and maintains military equipment using an official mission in Poland as cover. The deployment occurred without informing French lawmakers, amid a presidential election cycle where far-right figures propose cutting financial aid.
articles.description: The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026

articles.headline: Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab Strait leaving Houthis in control
articles.title: Yemeni forces retreat to defend port city from Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia withdrew from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait on November 15, 2026, leaving the waterway under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. The military redeployed troops to defend the interim capital of Aden. The seizure of the strait disrupted global oil exports and escalated a conflict that has displaced nearly 330,000 people, according to United Nations estimates cited in the report.
articles.description: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to protect the interim capital, Aden.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh reviews cyclone preparedness as 173 fishing boats remain at sea
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu evaluated state readiness on November 16, 2026, as the Bay of Bengal depression prepares to hit the coast as Cyclone Akvan by November 20. Agriculture officials urged farmers to secure 23.87 lakh hectares of crops. Meanwhile, authorities confirmed that 30,635 out of 30,808 fishing vessels returned safely, while search operations continue for the remaining boats.
articles.description: Andhra’s Agriculture Minister asks officials to help farmers harvest ready crops and move produce to safety before Cyclone Akvan

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Myanmar Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya ‘genocide’: Refugee crisis, timeline of the case, and more
articles.summary: The United Nations court in The Hague will issue a final ruling on November 19, 2026, regarding allegations that Myanmar committed genocide against the stateless Rohingya minority. Gambia initiated the lawsuit in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. The landmark case follows decades of sectarian violence, military crackdowns, and mass refugee exoduses into neighboring Bangladesh.
articles.description: The international community is closely watching the top UN court’s Rohingya verdict as an archetype for the case filed by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

articles.headline: US deploys USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier to the Middle East
articles.title: USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?
articles.summary: The United States military stationed the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East by November 15, 2026, bringing the total regional carrier strike groups to three. The deployment occurs while diplomatic negotiations involving Pakistan and Qatar remain stalled following a collapsed memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran earlier this year.
articles.description: The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command area of responsibility.

articles.headline: Russia stalls Ukraine talks with maximalist demands to fracture European security
articles.title: ‘NATO will collapse’: Russia stalls Ukraine talks, seeks to divide Europe
articles.summary: During United States-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian diplomats presented demands that go far beyond a peace settlement, seeking to dismantle Europe's post-Cold War security architecture. According to leaked documents and analysts, Moscow wants the North Atlantic Treaty Organization to withdraw troops from Central and Eastern Europe and sign individual nonaggression pacts that could undermine collective defense.
articles.description: Russia has proposed nonaggression pacts with individual nations, which could shatter collective defence against Moscow.

articles.headline: World Health Organization warns antimicrobial resistance could cause 39 million deaths
articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance could kill 39 million people over 25 years: WHO
articles.summary: The United Nations health agency stated that growing antimicrobial resistance threatens to make routine surgery and childbirth life-threatening if prevention and antibiotic use do not accelerate. Officials noted that drug-resistant infections were directly responsible for more than one million deaths in 2021 and released new diagnostic tools to help countries strengthen laboratory capabilities.
articles.description: UN's health agency says growing resistance to antibiotics and other medicines threatens 'future of modern medicine'.

articles.headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid tensions with Iran
articles.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid tensions with Iran
articles.description: Trump shares a message saying: ‘May God protect our troops’ as the USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Ukraine hits Russia's Crimea bridge in 1,300-drone barrage
articles.title: Ukraine hits Russia's Crimea bridge in 1,300-drone barrage
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched over thirteen hundred drones targeting Russian territory, successfully striking the Crimea bridge and causing minor damage that led to restricted traffic. Russian-installed governor Sergey Aksyonov confirmed the impact, while Moscow reported numerous interceptions. The aerial assault preceded an upcoming trilateral summit in Shenzhen involving world leaders discussing international security.
articles.description: The strike on the bridge appeared to inflict only minor damage, though drew an angry response from Russian-installed officials

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi travels to Manila for ASEAN and East Asia summits
articles.title: PM Modi arrives in Philippines to attend two key regional summits
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi traveled to Manila in the Philippines on November 16, 2026, to attend the 23rd Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Modi stated that ties with ASEAN form the core of India's Act East Policy. Quad leaders are also scheduled to meet on the sidelines on November 17, 2026, according to a senior United States official.
articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.

articles.headline: UK, Australia, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.title: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy issued a joint statement calling on Israel to permit immediate humanitarian access to Gaza, where recent floods have worsened conditions and thousands of tents remain held at the border. The conflict began after a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, resulting in tens of thousands of deaths during subsequent military operations.
articles.description: The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy say Israeli authorities are holding back vital supplies at the borders, including 150,00 tents.

articles.headline: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.title: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.summary: South African authorities are investigating two separate mass shootings that resulted in seventeen fatalities over the weekend. Nine victims were discovered inside a shack within an informal settlement in Pretoria, while eight others were found dead inside a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg. Police have not yet established a motive or made any arrests in connection with either incident.
articles.description: The ​motive for the shooting has not ⁠yet been established, and no arrests have been ‌made

articles.headline: China resists a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia
articles.title: Why is China resisting a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia?
articles.summary: Beijing remains hesitant to join any trilateral nuclear arms control treaty with the United States and Russia due to a significant disparity in warhead numbers. While Washington and Moscow possess thousands of weapons, China maintains a smaller, rapidly growing stockpile of approximately six hundred twenty warheads. Chinese officials emphasize their minimum deterrence posture and cite previous US withdrawals from key arms pacts.
articles.description: Beijing has a smaller arsenal than Washington and Moscow and worries that a pact could limit its nuclear capabilities.

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to return home in December
articles.title: Ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina says if death is the price to pay for returning home, she is ready to face it
articles.summary: Ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated she will return home in December despite facing a death sentence and numerous legal charges following her removal from power. Living in exile in India since fleeing a student-led uprising, she rejected the legitimacy of her trial and criticized Bangladeshi authorities for issuing threats instead of facilitating her voluntary repatriation.
articles.description: She was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on protesters

articles.headline: Prince and Princess of Wales arrive in India for official visit
articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales arrive in India ahead of meeting with Modi
articles.summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales have travelled to India for a three-day official visit, marking their first international trip together in four years. During the tour, Prince William and Catherine will attend events related to the Earthshot Prize and meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday to strengthen diplomatic ties between the nations.
articles.description: Most of the engagements the royal couple will attend are related to the Earthshot Prize, which Prince William founded.

articles.headline: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone approaches
articles.title: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone threat looms
articles.summary: The Odisha government directed district administrations on November 16, 2026, to begin early evacuations in southern regions as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified. The India Meteorological Department warns the system could strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm, reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast by November 19 and bringing heavy rainfall to Odisha.
articles.description: The weather system is likely to develop into a very severe cyclonic storm before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19 night

articles.headline: Russia's Andreeva defeats Ukraine's Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.title: Russia’s Andreeva defeats Ukraine’s Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win WTA Finals
articles.summary: Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva captured her first Women's Tennis Association Finals title by defeating Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina in straight sets in California. The match concluded without the traditional handshake, adhering to established Ukrainian policy. Andreeva earned millions and a luxury car, while Svitolina announced plans to return to Ukraine to support ongoing relief efforts.
articles.description: Mirra Andreeva won the final in straight sets to end her first Grand Slam-winning year as world number two.

articles.headline: Five European Union nations to unveil Rwanda migrant deportation hub deal
articles.title: European Union nations to unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
articles.summary: Five European Union nations including Germany and Denmark will announce an agreement on November 16, 2026, to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda. The pilot hub aims to host about one hundred people and facilitate repatriations. Human Rights Watch criticized the plan, citing concerns over Rwanda's human rights record, while officials hope the facility will be operational in 2027.
articles.description: The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the EU cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules

articles.headline: Global powers race to replace outgoing United Nations chief Antonio Guterres
articles.title: US and rivals spar over next UN boss as race lurches towards deadline
articles.summary: The race to replace outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is entering its final weeks ahead of a December 31 deadline. Eight candidates are competing amid geopolitical rivalries and opaque processes. Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan leads recent straw polls, though potential vetoes from permanent Security Council members pose hurdles to securing the position.
articles.description: Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan is the current frontrunner, polls suggest, but the US and Russia could veto her bid.

articles.headline: Estonia to close Russian border crossings following suspected sabotage attack
articles.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack
articles.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia starting December 1, 2026, according to Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna. The decision follows the detention of eight suspects over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems, which Tallinn blamed on Russian military intelligence. Moscow dismissed the accusations as another demonstration of Russophobia.
articles.description: Estonian authorities detained ‌eight people overnight on suspicion of an attempted arson attack on ‌drone maker Threod Systems that they ‌said ⁠had been ordered by Russia’s ⁠GRU military intelligence service

articles.headline: US proposed Ukraine cede Donbas parts for NATO membership
articles.title: US suggested Ukraine cede parts of Donbas to Russia to become part of NATO
articles.summary: United States negotiators suggested that Ukraine surrender parts of eastern Donbas in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking in remarks released on Saturday, Zelenskyy stated he refused to cede territory but indicated he would hold a national referendum if comprehensive security guarantees and reconstruction funds were provided by international partners.
articles.description: Zelenskyy rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality and said he refused to cede territory to Russia.

articles.headline: Trump considers holding off on further attacks against Iran
articles.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has told advisers that he may delay further military action against Iran if Tehran and its allies commit no new provocations, according to three sources. Regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan urged the president during phone calls to avoid escalating the conflict further.
articles.description: The war has hiked global fuel prices and proven unpopular with U.S. voters, who handed control ‌of ⁠Congress to the Democrats in last week's midterm elections

articles.headline: England defeat Spain 3-2 to secure top spot in group A3
articles.title: England stun Spain 3-2 to end record unbeaten streak
articles.summary: England defeated world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid on November 16, 2026, ending La Roja's record forty-four match unbeaten run in competitive games. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White secured the victory, while Spain responded through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. England finished as group winners in Nations League group A3 despite playing with ten men following Elliot Anderson's second-half red card, according to the report.
articles.description: Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja's first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat

articles.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months into response
articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.summary: Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, government data shows over eleven thousand cases and nearly half of those infected have died. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, eighty percent of new cases are detected outside health surveillance. Children and frontline workers face severe risks amid conflict and attacks in eastern provinces.
articles.description: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

articles.headline: World Health Organisation warns of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza
articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.summary: The World Health Organisation reported that acute respiratory infections in Gaza have risen by 33,000 cases compared to last year. Dr Reinhilde Van De Weerdt stated that heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians, worsening overcrowding and living conditions. The agency warned that the situation will deteriorate further during winter, while Israeli military agencies maintained that winterisation supplies and medical equipment have been facilitated into the region.
articles.description: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

articles.headline: India health expenditure triples as household out-of-pocket spending declines
articles.title: India’s health spending triples to ₹4.14 lakh crore, but out-of-pocket share drops to 42.7%: NHA
articles.summary: India's Union government health expenditure increased from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-2014 to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-2024, according to National Health Accounts estimates. The Health Ministry reported that the proportion of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade. The data highlights expanded public financing, increased primary healthcare spending, and growth in government and private health insurance schemes across the country.
articles.description: The share of healthcare costs borne by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over a decade, while social security spending on health rose from 6% to 11%

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva defeats Elina Svitolina to claim WTA Finals title
articles.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina to win WTA Finals; ascends to No. 2 in rankings
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 on November 15, 2026, to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Andreeva earned 3.37 million dollars and a Mercedes-Benz convertible, rising to number two in the world rankings. Svitolina collected 1.5 million dollars after finishing as the runner-up in the eight-day tournament, according to the match report.
articles.description: The WTA Finals win helped Mirra Andreeva to clinch her career-high ranking, just behing Elena Rybakina

articles.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin plan to hold a trilateral meeting next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, according to White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales. The leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers will discuss reducing nuclear weapons and the war in Iran, while bilateral talks are also scheduled between Trump and Xi.
articles.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

articles.headline: Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if U.S. trade talks fail
articles.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in Cambodia on November 16, 2026, that Canada could pursue alternative partnerships with Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with United States President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Carney emphasized that Washington talks remain his priority following a January agreement that permitted limited Chinese electric vehicles into Canada under reduced tariffs.
articles.description: Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

articles.headline: Protests erupt in Gopalganj over proposed return of ousted leader Hasina
articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Supporters of ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged violent demonstrations in Gopalganj on November 15, 2026, demanding her return from India. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity. The unrest prompted the government to withdraw local officials and deploy paramilitary forces to maintain public order.
articles.description: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

articles.headline: US government seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta
articles.title: U.S. govt seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder-for-hire plot
articles.summary: United States authorities are pushing for a 24-year prison sentence for Indian national Nikhil Gupta over his involvement in a foiled plot to assassinate American citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Gupta previously pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire charges and is scheduled to be sentenced on November 20 by United States District Judge Victor Marrero.
articles.description: Gupta will be sentenced on November 20. His lawyers have, however, argued for a "substantial downward" sentence of 12 years' imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release

articles.headline: Nvidia must hire outside chief executive after Huang departure, Bessent says
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Scott Bessent wants answers soon from Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia must hire an outside chief executive following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12, 2026, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent added that the board and outside counsel must answer questions regarding export compliance within 10 days.
articles.description: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China

articles.headline: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.title: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.description: An advance by the Houthi armed group in Yemen is threatening one of the government’s last strongholds.

articles.headline: Megaspeed launches internal investigation into business and supply chain
articles.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced an internal investigation into its business operations after executive Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, left her role in August 2025. The company stated it complies with all regulatory regimes, while US treasury and commerce officials face mounting congressional scrutiny over high-end AI chip exports.
articles.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.

articles.headline: US aviation authorities investigate nationwide ground stop caused by equipment failure
articles.title: After a nationwide ground stop, US faces aviation infrastructure questions
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded United States flights for nearly four hours following a router malfunction during an upgrade performed by defence contractor L3Harris. Over 9,000 flights were cancelled and 1.5 million passengers stranded. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that investigations are ongoing into the incident, which has also renewed scrutiny regarding ageing infrastructure across the national aviation system.
articles.description: Trump has requested $50bn for upgrades, but Democratic lawmakers are asking for transparency before spending more.

articles.headline: India offers extended service terms to military recruits under Agnipath scheme
articles.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Defence announced on 4 November that soldiers finishing four-year terms under the Agnipath programme can serve two additional years at higher pay. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani stated the decision followed internal reviews. More than 18,300 recruits will complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026, amid ongoing debates regarding training duration and military effectiveness.
articles.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

articles.headline: US proposes Ukraine cedes territory for NATO membership, says Zelensky
articles.title: U.S. proposes Ukraine cede territory in exchange for joining NATO: Zelensky
articles.summary: United States officials suggested for the first time that Ukraine should cede land to Russia in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Moscow rejected an energy target ceasefire during talks in Abu Dhabi. He emphasized that any decision regarding territorial concessions would require societal approval following confirmation of security guarantees.
articles.description: Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had rejected a ceasefire on energy targets at talks in Abu Dhabi, as Moscow was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold trilateral meeting at APEC summit
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will participate in their first trilateral meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Discussions will primarily address nuclear proliferation, notably the expired New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty. The gathering also occurs amid ongoing geopolitical tensions concerning conflicts in Ukraine and Iran alongside bilateral trade disputes.
articles.description: A nuclear treaty and the US's war on Iran are among priority topics for China, Russia and US leaders.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden
articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces announced a strategic withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait area to prioritize the defense of Aden. The retreat on November 15, 2026, marks the end of a six-week counteroffensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, who previously seized the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that the Houthis released 600 prisoners on the same day amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

articles.headline: Thousands of US flights face cancellations following technical failure
articles.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
articles.summary: Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed after a technical failure in a communication router caused a national ground stop. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy stated normal operations may take time to recover as aircraft remain out of position. President Donald Trump urged Congress to approve funding to modernise the system.
articles.description: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot calls for Benjamin Netanyahu's removal amid alleged election meddling
articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded the immediate departure of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following allegations of electoral interference reported by broadcaster Channel 12 on Sunday. The report claimed Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, improperly prompted police raids against Ra'am party members before the October 27 election. Netanyahu's Likud party condemned the remarks as outrageous incitement.
articles.description: Arab party members were reportedly arrested before Israeli elections based on unfounded evidence from the PM's office.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strike kills three in Russia amid NATO territory claims
articles.title: Three killed in Russia as Ukraine claims US floated NATO membership option
articles.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed a family of three in the Russian border region of Belgorod, according to local authorities. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that United States negotiators raised the possibility of ceding eastern territory for North Atlantic Treaty Organization membership during recent talks in Abu Dhabi, though Kyiv rejected any immediate withdrawal from the Donbas region.
articles.description: Zelenskyy says the US asked for the first time whether Kyiv would cede land to Moscow in exchange for the NATO bid.

articles.headline: US media implicates former Indian intelligence chief in Pannun plot
articles.title: U.S. media names Indian official who allegedly ordered plot on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
articles.summary: United States authorities assessed that an alleged assassination plot against Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun was directed by the former chief of India's Research and Analysis Wing, Samant Goel. According to a report by the Washington Post, officials believe the operation received official sanction from individuals connected to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the allegations.
articles.description: According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

articles.headline: Amaravati develops indigenous quantum technology stack to build local computers
articles.title: Amaravati builds indigenous quantum tech stack
articles.summary: An expanding network of companies, universities, and startups in Amaravati is developing domestic quantum technologies to foster local manufacturing. According to state officials, regional entities have created the NAADA resonator chip, the Q-SHIVA cryogenic platform, Q-CoRE control electronics, and Q-CODE software. These innovations aim to reduce import reliance and establish the region as a global quantum development hub.
articles.description: Amaravati-based companies, universities and startups develop the NAADA chip, Q-SHIVA cryogenic platform, Q-CoRE electronics and Q-CODE software, laying the foundation for building quantum computers locally

articles.headline: Investigation identifies Benjamin Tait as the operator behind anonymous X account
articles.title: Who is behind Habibi UK, an X account that targeted critics of Israel?
articles.summary: A six-month investigation by the Byline Times identified Benjamin Tait, a 61-year-old former United States Foreign Service officer, as the operator of the anonymous X account Habibi UK. The account targeted critics of Israel with online attacks and was amplified by various political figures. Tait previously directed a political campaign firm and operated an energy research company before its liquidation.
articles.description: A former US Foreign Service officer ran a company that funded election adverts attacking Jeremy Corbyn’s Labour.

articles.headline: Thiruvananthapuram court finds eleven CPI(M) workers guilty in RSS activist murder
articles.title: Keralam RSS activist Ranjith murder case: 11 CPI(M) workers found guilty
articles.summary: The Thiruvananthapuram Additional District and Sessions Court found eleven Communist Party of India Marxist workers guilty in the 2008 murder of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh activist Ranjith in Mannanthala. Prosecutors established that political hostility following the killing of another activist motivated the attack. The court cancelled the convicts' bails and scheduled their sentencing for the following day.
articles.description: Thiruvananthapuram court to pronounce sentences on November 18

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi questions EC’s ‘unanimous’ SIR decision ahead of Supreme Court hearing
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi questions EC’s ‘unanimous’ SIR decision ahead of Supreme Court hearing
articles.description: A day before the Supreme Court resumes hearing challenges to the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, Rahul Gandhi has questioned the poll body’s claim that the programme was approved unanimously by all three Election Commissioners.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh puts coastal districts on high alert for Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Andhra Home Minister Anitha puts coastal districts on high alert, warns fishermen
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha ordered all coastal districts into high alert as Cyclone Akvan approaches the Bay of Bengal. During a review meeting with disaster management officials, authorities warned that the storm is projected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm before crossing the coast on Friday, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha asks people to stay alert over the next four days and the Agriculture Department to help farmers protect crops ready for harvest

articles.headline: Kulgam anti-terror operations continue as security forces retrieve body of accomplice
articles.title: Kulgam anti-terror ops continue; body of LeT terrorist Latteef Bhat’s ‘accomplice’ retrieved from encounter site
articles.summary: Security forces in Kulgam continued anti-terror operations for the seventh consecutive day while retrieving the body of an alleged accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat from an encounter site. Local political parties criticized the prolonged security restrictions and civilian hardships resulting from the operations following a recent checkpoint attack that injured three personnel.
articles.description: Security agencies released CCTV footage, which suggested Dar and Bhat were seen together on November 10 and 11 surveying multiple locations

articles.headline: Civil society questions Telangana police detention of SIO members over Israel event
articles.title: Civil society questions detention of SIO members over their stance on Telangana-Israel collaboration event
articles.summary: Civil society members in Hyderabad accused the Telangana police of curtailing democratic rights following the preventative detention of Students Islamic Organisation members on November 16, 2026. Activists including Padmaja Shaw and Khalida Parveen criticized the action as a human rights violation targeting Muslim youth who questioned a government collaboration with Israeli entities at T-Hub.
articles.description: Civil society members said that the detentions were contrary to India’s consistent foreign policy of supporting Palestine

articles.headline: Union Minister Santanu Thakur comments on political violence in West Bengal
articles.title: Feuds, factions and allegations of extortion: BJP’s problem of plenty in West Bengal | Explained
articles.summary: Union Minister of State Santanu Thakur remarked that party supporters are both perpetrators and victims of political violence in West Bengal. Speaking on November 15, 2026, the minister highlighted the shifting political dynamics six months after the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power in the state, following earlier remarks by state party president Samik Bhattacharya during the assembly election campaign.
articles.description: The BJP leadership in West Bengal is not only facing the challenge of dealing with factionalism but also allegations of extortion by a section of its leaders

articles.headline: Alappuzha authorities to cull 26000 birds following bird flu confirmation
articles.title: Bird flu confirmed at two farms in Keralam’s Alappuzha; 26,000 birds to be culled
articles.summary: Authorities in Keralam will begin culling approximately 26,000 domestic birds on November 18, 2026, after bird flu was confirmed at two poultry farms in Alappuzha district. The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal verified the infection in samples. District Collector Shaji V Nair convened an emergency meeting to coordinate six rapid response teams within the surveillance zone.
articles.description: Six rapid response teams of Animal Husbandry and Health departments set to carry out culling

articles.headline: Pakistan and Iran stress sustained coordination for regional stability in Rawalpindi
articles.title: Pakistan, Iran stress sustained engagement, coordination for regional stability
articles.summary: Pakistan Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir met with an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi on November 16, 2026, to discuss regional stability and security challenges. Mr. Araghchi also attended the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting and held talks with Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar regarding diplomatic engagement.
articles.description: Field Marshal Munir made the remarks during a meeting with a high-level Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear Rahul Gandhi application regarding election commission affidavit
articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to hear an application filed by Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders posing forty-eight interrogatories to Election Commission of India officials. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant scheduled the hearing for December 9, 2026, following challenges to an October 26 affidavit concerning the nationwide service information report exercise that excluded approximately thirteen crore voters.
articles.description: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

articles.headline: Indian Oil Corporation secures government approval for commercial sustainable aviation fuel supply
articles.title: IOC gets government nod for commercial sustainable aviation fuel supply from Panipat refinery
articles.summary: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation obtained government approvals to commercially supply sustainable aviation fuel from its Panipat refinery, Chairman A.S. Sahney announced on November 17, 2026. The facility aims to meet India's 1 per cent blending target for international flights in 2027 by producing about 35,000 tonnes annually from used cooking oil sourced from large hospitality chains.
articles.description: The State-run refiner plans to enter into supply agreements with airlines before committing investments to additional SAF projects

articles.headline: Four nations urge Israel to allow immediate humanitarian aid into Gaza
articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
articles.summary: Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom urged Israel to permit immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza following severe floods. The foreign ministers noted that 150,000 tents and vital supplies remain restricted at the border. More than 1.9 million people have been displaced in the territory during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The countries accuse Israel of preventing tents and other supplies from entering Gaza, despite the humanitarian crisis.

articles.headline: Denmark expands industrial biogas production using livestock manure to drive energy transition
articles.title: Powering towns on pig manure: How Denmark has transformed energy generation
articles.summary: Denmark has developed approximately 150 industrial-sized biogas plants utilizing livestock manure to supply about 40 percent of its national gas grid. While the sector aids energy independence and decarbonization initiatives such as Sonderborg's ProjectZero, critics argue the reliance on manure perpetuates factory farming, prompting ongoing debates over agricultural emissions and upcoming carbon taxes.
articles.description: Pigs are big business in Denmark. Now their waste is being turned into biogas, which powers the national grid.

articles.headline: Bessent calls for outsider leadership at Nvidia following executive scandal
articles.title: US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocated for external leadership at Nvidia during a television appearance on November 15, 2026. The technology firm faces scrutiny after former chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. Bessent also called for a 10-day deadline to verify export compliance.
articles.description: Scott Bessent gives Nvidia's board 10 days to show the company's compliance with US export controls.

articles.headline: India prepares for opening Test match against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ Tests: India faces test of character as WTC hopes hang in balance
articles.summary: India faces New Zealand in the opening Test match of a two-match series at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 17, 2026. The series carries significant implications for India's qualification hopes for the World Test Championship final and its quest for a first series victory in New Zealand in 17 years. Captain Shubman Gill indicated the team may select four pace-bowling options for the match.
articles.description: After winning the T20I and ODI series, India turn their attention to the Tests. With conditions favouring pace, Gill and the team management must balance bowling firepower with batting depth

articles.headline: Israeli opposition targets Knesset speaker role to advance legislative agenda
articles.title: As Knesset readies for new speaker, Israeli opposition holds powerful role
articles.summary: Following the November election, the Israeli political opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot seeks to elect Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker on Tuesday with the support of Arab-led parties. Securing this powerful legislative post would allow the anti-Netanyahu bloc to introduce key measures, including an inquiry into the October 7, 2023, attacks, restoring attorney general powers, and proposing a premiership term limit while coalition talks continue.
articles.description: The anti-Netanyahu bloc holds the keys to electing a new parliamentary speaker, setting the momentum for change.

articles.headline: Mozambique opposition leader Venancio Mondlane faces trial over election unrest
articles.title: Mozambique opposition leader faces trial over deadly 2024 election unrest
articles.summary: Prominent Mozambican opposition leader Venancio Mondlane appeared in the Supreme Court in Maputo to face trial on charges including incitement to terrorism and civil disobedience. The proceedings follow deadly post-election protests stemming from disputed presidential results in 2024 that declared Daniel Chapo the winner. Rights groups reported over three hundred deaths during the subsequent unrest, while police recorded ninety-six fatalities.
articles.description: Venâncio Mondlane faces several charges over 2024 post-election protests that left hundreds of people dead.

articles.headline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits the oldest Philippine gurudwara
articles.title: PM Modi leads foundation stone-laying ceremony for Philippines’ oldest gurudwara’s redevelopment
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the century-old Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila and led the foundation stone-laying ceremony for its redevelopment project. Mr. Modi is currently on a three-day visit to the Philippines to attend regional summits including the ASEAN-India meeting, aiming to strengthen diplomatic ties and cultural connections across Southeast Asia.
articles.description: PM Narendra Modi, who is on a three-day visit to the Philippines, said he felt "very blessed" to visit the over a century-old Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila

articles.headline: India plans four-pacercorps for opening Test against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ Tests: India set to unleash four-pronged pace attack
articles.summary: Captain Shubman Gill confirmed that the visiting team will deploy four frontline fast bowlers for the opening Test match against New Zealand beginning in Wellington on November 19, 2026. Jasprit Bumrah will lead the pace attack alongside Mohammed Siraj, while the team finalises remaining selections to handle pitch conditions and strong winds during the two-match series opener.
articles.description: The nature of the Basin Reserve surface and the demands of bowling in Wellington’s notorious winds have added to the selection conundrum

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court initiates criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee
articles.title: Calcutta High Court issues criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court initiated criminal contempt proceedings against Trinamool Congress leader and parliamentarian Abhishek Banerjee following remarks and social media posts that allegedly scandalised the judiciary. Justice Krishna Rao directed the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within fifteen days why appropriate action should not be taken against him over statements made regarding protection and election outcomes.
articles.description: Justice Krishna Rao had said that by his remarks on November 7, Abhishek Banerjee had committed criminal contempt of the court” and “attempted with interference of administration of justice

articles.headline: Supreme Court Bar Association seeks contempt action against lawyer over derogatory remarks
articles.title: SCBA seeks contempt action against lawyer for derogatory remarks about CJI
articles.summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association informed the Supreme Court on November 17, 2026, that it intends to pursue contempt proceedings against a lawyer who made derogatory remarks about Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. Association representatives stated that the attorney general granted statutory consent for the petition. The chief justice agreed to list the matter for November 18 upon completion of procedural requirements.
articles.description: The office bearers urged the court to tag the petition along with pending contempt pleas against journalist Nikhil Wagle and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut

articles.headline: Israel restricts aid entry as winter storms batter Gaza
articles.title: Who can force Israel to implement Gaza ceasefire deal?
articles.summary: Palestinians in Gaza face harsh winter weather in tents without basic services while Israel restricts humanitarian aid entry. Calls from the United Nations, European Union and the US-established Board of Peace have gone unanswered, leaving displaced families vulnerable to flooding and cold conditions, according to the report.
articles.description: Storms batter Palestinian territory as Israel restricts entry of aid.

articles.headline: Caste and political rivalries emerge ahead of elections
articles.title: Caste, old rivalries and Uttarakhand’s shadow on U.P. Assembly poll
articles.summary: Recent verbal exchanges between Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav highlight critical caste and political equations connecting Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Carved out in 2000 under Bharatiya Janata Party rule, Uttarakhand is scheduled to hold legislative assembly elections alongside Uttar Pradesh during the February to March 2027 electoral cycle.
articles.description: By invoking the Rajput connection, CM Adityanath has inadvertently brought alive memories of a past when it suited the interests of the two parties to keep the Congress out

articles.headline: South Korea cracks down on AI exam cheating after top scorer confession
articles.title: South Korea cheating scandal: Are AI smart glasses a threat to exams?
articles.summary: South Korean authorities are tightening security measures for annual college entrance exams following an online confession by a top-scoring student who used artificial intelligence and a miniature camera to cheat. Prime Minister Han Seok-sook called an emergency meeting to address the scandal, prompting the Ministry of Education to announce strict eyewear inspections and potential criminal penalties for future offenders.
articles.description: A student with near-perfect scores on two tests has confessed to using artificial intelligence.

articles.headline: Baidu CEO warns of artificial intelligence bubble ahead of APEC meetings
articles.title: Head of China’s Baidu warns of AI ‘bubble’ ahead of APEC talks
articles.summary: Chinese technology giant Baidu Chief Executive Officer Robin Li stated that artificial intelligence adoption has failed to boost profits for most companies, raising concerns about a potential market bubble. Speaking in Shenzhen during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting, Mr. Li noted that application-layer penetration has fallen short of expectations amid ongoing global industry challenges and broader financial risks.
articles.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to hold talks with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday during APEC

articles.headline: Congress criticizes Census 2027 process as a farce
articles.title: Census 2027 turning out to be farce: Congress
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress criticized the Census 2027 process on November 17, 2026, citing grave implications over data collection procedures. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh highlighted that the self-enumeration portal briefly listed sects and spiritual figures among religious categories before removal, while also noting the absence of proper dropdown menus for non-scheduled castes.
articles.description: Census 2027 is turning out to be a farce in many respects. This will have grave implications, Jairam Ramesh said

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan brews over Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan brews over Bay of Bengal: What you need to know
articles.summary: A weather system intensified into Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the Bay of Bengal on November 16, 2026, moving towards Andhra Pradesh, according to the Indian Meteorological Department. The storm is forecast to become a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the coast on November 20. Heavy rainfall warnings were issued for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, prompting authorities to halt marine operations.
articles.description: Cyclone Akvan may intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026)

articles.headline: AI models abandon climate facts to please users, UNESCO report finds
articles.title: AI models abandon climate facts to please users, UNESCO report finds
articles.description: AI models abandon climate facts to agree with users in eight out of 10 tests.

articles.headline: North Korean leader visits ski resort while Donald Trump hints at meeting
articles.title: North Korea’s Kim visits ski resort as Donald Trump hints at possible meeting
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited a northern tourist zone near the Chinese border, according to state media reports released by the official Korean Central News Agency. Meanwhile, United States President Donald Trump suggested a possible meeting with Mr. Kim during a diplomatic tour, though regional experts indicate no visible preparations for such discussions are currently underway.
articles.description: We may meet with Kim Jong Un also, so that'll be good, Donald Trump told reporters

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo remains uncontrolled
articles.title: Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to battle an uncontrolled Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain, recording over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths since May. Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya stated that delayed detection, conflict and a funding shortfall have hindered containment efforts, though the World Health Organization is advancing clinical trials.
articles.description: 'If we don't stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak,' Africa ​CDC director says.

articles.headline: Andy Burnham says Brexit is what the UK’s ‘enemies’ wanted
articles.title: Andy Burnham says Brexit is what the UK’s ‘enemies’ wanted
articles.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham slammed Brexit in a speech at the Lord Mayor’s Banquet.

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister D.K. Shivakumar outlines tech expansion goals
articles.title: Karnataka charting next tech leap to push AI, deep-tech: CM D.K. Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka aims to become a global hub for artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing, according to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 17, 2026. Speaking in Bengaluru, he noted the State attracted $9.4 billion in foreign direct investment equity during the first half of fiscal year 2025-26. The government plans new initiatives, including a government-driven artificial intelligence university and semiconductor facility investments exceeding ₹23,000 crore.
articles.description: Inaugurating the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar unveils major infrastructure, funding, and reskilling initiatives to lead global innovation beyond artificial intelligence

articles.headline: Microsoft infrastructure issue causes worldwide Microsoft 365 and Outlook outages
articles.title: How does India address service outages?
articles.summary: An unspecific network upgrade failure within Microsoft infrastructure impacted global access to productivity tools like Microsoft 365 and Outlook between November 12 and November 13, 2026. Indian carriers including IndiGo, Akasa Air, and Air India experienced email support disruptions and rerouting as a consequence of the technical fault, according to company statements released on November 17, 2026.
articles.description: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite? What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form? How are cloud companies accountable in other countries? What are Indian customers’ options?

articles.headline: U.S. lawmakers and officials welcome court ruling on visa fee
articles.title: U.S. lawmakers welcome court order scrapping $100,000 H-1B visa fee
articles.summary: United States lawmakers and state officials welcomed a federal court order striking down a $100,000 fee on H-1B visa applications on June 9, 2026. Massachusetts federal judge Leo Sorokin ruled the fee unlawful for lacking congressional approval, following a lawsuit led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers indicated the administration plans to appeal the decision in an appellate court.
articles.description: Republican lawmakers focused on H-1B visas for healthcare workers and teachers who are in short supply particularly in rural areas, rather than on the IT sector, which benefits from this visa category

articles.headline: Ukraine President Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink speed restrictions
articles.title: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that military satellite internet speeds remain restricted, hindering efforts to intercept Russian attacks. Speaking on Sunday, Zelensky said terminals operated by Elon Musk's Starshield system lost connection at speeds exceeding 161km/h. Meanwhile, regional officials reported ongoing Russian strikes resulting in multiple fatalities across Ukrainian regions including Chernihiv and Luhansk, while Ukraine launched retaliatory drone attacks on industrial sites in Russia.
articles.description: The Ukrainian president says the slowed-down internet is making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.

articles.headline: Software bug at JPMorgan Chase causes banking transaction delays
articles.title: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
articles.summary: A technical hardware issue at JPMorgan Chase created widespread transaction delays across major American financial systems and Zelle on Monday. The bank stated that the internal software bug was not a cyberattack and assured customers that funds remained accessible while engineers worked to restore normal operations before the end of the day.
articles.description: Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.

articles.headline: US Congress considers stricter AI chip export rules after Nvidia scandal
articles.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: Lawmakers from both parties are pursuing stricter export rules on artificial intelligence chips following a scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. Senate leaders and House Speaker Mike Johnson have called for congressional testimony and renewed support for legislative measures limiting chip exports to China.
articles.description: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress. Senate Minority […]

articles.headline: UEFA backs French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo against Gianni Infantino
articles.title: UEFA backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
articles.summary: European football governing body UEFA announced on November 16, 2026, its unanimous backing for French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo to contest the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Diallo accepted the invitation to challenge incumbent Gianni Infantino at the congress scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat. The European association previously expressed strong opposition to Infantino regarding controversial governance proposals.
articles.description: UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in the election, which will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year

articles.headline: Gas leak at ONGC well in Andhra Pradesh triggers evacuations
articles.title: Gas leak at ONGC well in Andhra’s Konaseema; residents within 1 km alerted, road closed
articles.summary: Authorities evacuated residents within a one-kilometre radius after a natural gas leak occurred during drilling at an Oil and Natural Gas Corporation well near Nagaram village on November 17, 2026. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to ensure public safety and deploy specialised technical teams to cap the well, while traffic on nearby roads was blocked as a precaution against potential hazards.
articles.description: There is no blowout or fire so far, officials say; experts are on their way to plug the leak

articles.headline: Two people killed in two-storey building collapse in Delhi
articles.title: Two killed, four injured as building collapses in Delhi’s Jwala Nagar
articles.summary: A three-year-old girl and a thirty-year-old man died while four other tenants sustained injuries following the collapse of a two-storey residential building in east Delhi on November 17, 2026. Police personnel and emergency services rescued all trapped occupants from the debris in the Jwala Nagar area, transporting them to Hedgewar Hospital for medical treatment while an investigation commenced.
articles.description: A three-year-old girl among the deceased; six tenants rescued from the debris and taken to Hedgewar Hospital

articles.headline: Quad leaders gather in Manila for strategic Indo-Pacific summit
articles.title: What is Quad, what is on the Manila agenda, and why does the 2026 summit matter?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will join leaders from the United States, Japan, and Australia in Manila on November 17, 2026, for the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue summit. The meeting will address critical mineral supply chains, commercial shipping security, and regional stability in the Indo-Pacific, marking the first time the summit is hosted by a non-member nation.
articles.description: The summit in Manila will be the first meeting of Quad leaders since they gathered in Wilmington, United States, in September 2024

articles.headline: Wayanad selected to host India mountain ecology congress
articles.title: Wayanad set to host Processual Mountains, India’s first mountain ecology congress
articles.summary: Researchers, policymakers, and indigenous communities will gather in Wayanad for India's first mountain ecology congress from December 10 to 12, 2026. Organised by the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology and the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University at Pookode, the event will address ecological vulnerability, disaster management, and sustainable development across mountain regions.
articles.description: Event brings together researchers, policymakers, indigenous communities and mountain practitioners to discuss the changing ecology, cultures and future of mountain regions

articles.headline: Rohit Pawar questions Devendra Fadnavis over VSR Ventures links
articles.title: Ajit Pawar plane crash: Rohit Pawar questions CM Devendra Fadnavis’ links with VSR Ventures
articles.summary: Nationalist Congress Party Sharad Pawar faction leader Rohit Pawar alleged on November 16, 2026, that Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis is protecting VSR Ventures, the aviation firm linked to the plane crash that killed former Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar. Bharatiya Janata Party leaders dismissed the claims as politically motivated publicity stunts and defended the Chief Minister against the accusations.
articles.description: Presenting a 49-page slideshow containing photographs, videos, flight records and documents, Mr. Pawar questioned why an FIR had not been registered in Maharashtra despite repeated complaints and why the investigation had not been handed over to the CBI

articles.headline: Estonia closes border crossings with Russia after attempted arson attack
articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
articles.summary: Estonian authorities announced the closure of border crossings with Russia following an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated on Sunday that eight individuals were detained over the incident, which Tallinn attributes to Russian military intelligence. Latvian Interior Minister Janis Dombrava confirmed several arrests involving local citizens. Officials stated the measure aims to curb hostile activities and prevent sanctions circumvention by Moscow.
articles.description: Eight arrests made in connection with an attempted arson, which Tallinn says was ordered by Russian intelligence.

articles.headline: Southeast Asian leaders extend Myanmar ban over failure to implement peace plan
articles.title: Southeast Asian leaders denounce violence in Myanmar, extend ban on its leader
articles.summary: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations meeting in Manila on Sunday extended a ban on Myanmar's leader attending regional summits. The bloc stated that the military-backed government in Myanmar has failed to comply with the 2021 five-point peace plan and continues to attack civilians. Under the restrictions, Myanmar may only be represented by lower-level career diplomats during the ongoing three-day summit addressing regional conflicts.
articles.description: ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi
