articles.title: Doctor held for ‘sexually harassing’ house surgeon in Keralam
articles.summary: Police took a government doctor into custody following allegations that he made sexual advances toward a postgraduate house surgeon at Nedumangad Government Taluk Hospital. Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan stated that strict disciplinary measures will be implemented against the accused. The arrest occurred at the suspect residence following the recording of the victim detailed statement and subsequent protests by workers.
articles.description: Health Minister promises action in the incident

articles.headline: TRAI bars over 1.24 lakh mobile connections in spam crackdown
articles.title: TRAI crackdown on spam: Over 1.24 lakh mobile connections barred or disconnected in July-September
articles.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India enforced punitive measures against more than 1.24 lakh telecom resources and blacklisted 374 entities during the July-September period to combat unsolicited commercial communications. Officials reported receiving 15.29 lakh complaints through channels including the DND application. Telecom operators deployed artificial intelligence systems that flagged billions of incoming calls and messages as suspected spam throughout the quarter.
articles.description: A total of 1,10,325 telecom resources, including mobile numbers, were barred from outgoing services for 15 days for the first violation

articles.headline: Students protest at SRFTI after filmmaker Ronny Sen denied entry
articles.title: Row erupts at SRFTI over denial of entry to filmmaker Ronny Sen
articles.summary: A campus dispute intensified at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute after students accused the administration of blocking filmmaker Ronny Sen from conducting a workshop. Institute authorities stated that the Emmy-nominated director entered the premises unlawfully by scaling the perimeter wall. The confrontation follows ongoing student protests and the suspension of classes at the institute until December 11.
articles.description: SRFTI has been on the boil since September 27, when a clash broke out between a section of students and members of a right-wing organisation who were holding an event inside the institute’s auditorium

articles.headline: Indian apparel exports increase 20 percent in October
articles.title: Apparel exports surge 20% in October on currency depreciation, but volume growth remains subdued
articles.summary: Apparel exports from India grew 20.33 percent in dollar terms during October compared to the previous year, primarily driven by currency depreciation rather than shipment volume growth. Apparel Export Promotion Council Chairman A Sakthivel noted that the performance signals a gradual recovery in international demand. Major destinations for these ready-made garments continued to include the United States, the United Kingdom, and the United Arab Emirates.

articles.headline: Centre launches portal for mandatory online rice and paddy stock declaration
articles.title: Centre operationalises portal for online declaration of rice, paddy stock
articles.summary: The Union Food Ministry launched an online portal requiring all traders, retailers, wholesalers, and millers to declare their paddy and rice inventories weekly to prevent hoarding and control inflation. Entities failing to register or comply with stock limits will face penalties under the Essential Commodities Act. Retail rice inflation previously reached 8.25 percent in September, driven by reduced kharif paddy acreage and deficient rainfall.
articles.description: Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955

articles.headline: BMRCL to run 13 trains daily on Yellow Line from November 16
articles.title: Bengaluru Metro’s Yellow Line to run 13 trains daily from November 16; peak-hour frequency cut to 5.5 minutes
articles.summary: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited announced the addition of a new train to its service on the Yellow Line, bringing the daily operational total to 13 trains. This adjustment improves weekday peak-hour frequency from six minutes to 5.5 minutes while maintaining regular schedules during non-peak hours and weekends across the designated transport network.

articles.headline: Union Minister calls for coordinated anti-pollution measures across Delhi-NCR
articles.title: Air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, coordinated action required: Union Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav urged regional authorities to enforce stricter pollution controls across the National Capital Region. Speaking at a review meeting, he stressed the importance of real-time monitoring, designated state officials, and automated camera surveillance to address severe air quality concerns and reduce vehicle emissions.
articles.description: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground

articles.headline: Kerala High Court rules Tantri holds no ownership over deity assets
articles.title: Tantri does not have ownership of assets belonging to deity, says Kerala HC
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court determined that a temple Tantri possesses authority solely over religious rituals rather than legal ownership of deity assets. A division bench comprising Justices K.V. Jayakumar and Raja Vijayaraghavan V. dismissed a petition challenging a 2012 circular from the Travancore Devaswom Board, upholding statutory management frameworks for temple properties.
articles.description: The authority to perform and supervise religious ceremonies must be distinguished from the right to own or deal with the property of the deity, the court observes

articles.headline: Surging onion prices create severe financial distress for consumers in Kochi
articles.title: Surge in onion prices hits consumers hard
articles.summary: Retail markets in Kochi experienced a significant spike in onion prices, with shallots reaching up to ₹180 per kilogram due to low yields and supply shortages from Tamil Nadu. Local vendors reported that household budgets are strained by elevated costs for essential vegetables and provisions, which traders indicate are unlikely to stabilise until January.
articles.description: One kilogram of shallots costs up to ₹180 in the retail market in Kochi. The price of the essential item is around ₹50 per kg higher than it was the previous month, say traders.

articles.headline: Nigeria cautions citizens against travelling through Ethiopia's high-altitude international airport
articles.title: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
articles.summary: The Nigerian government has advised travellers, especially those with pre-existing medical issues, to exercise caution when transiting through Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa. The foreign ministry in Abuja reported that 16 Nigerians with underlying health problems died this year while passing through the high-altitude Ethiopian capital. Officials noted that lower oxygen levels at 2,334 metres above sea level pose serious risks to cardiovascular and respiratory health.
articles.description: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.

articles.headline: Noel Tata cautions against listing Tata Sons to preserve operating philosophy
articles.title: Why to tinker with something that has delivered value for 150 years: Noel Tata
articles.summary: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has expressed opposition to listing Tata Sons, warning that shareholder interests could eventually supersede philanthropy and alter the group's governance model. Speaking in New Delhi, he emphasized that charity takes precedence over commerce within the 150-year-old conglomerate. While addressing calls for a public listing amid regulatory requirements from the Reserve Bank of India, he stressed the importance of maintaining institutional continuity and operational discipline.
articles.description: The trusts will work with regulators to find a solution to keep the Tata way as it is

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israeli forces occupy Palestinian-American’s home
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israeli forces occupy Palestinian-American’s home
articles.description: Israeli forces occupied a Palestinian-American’s home in the occupied West Bank for 17 days.

articles.headline: NASA space probe Voyager 1 approaches milestone of one light-day distance
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 to hit new space distance record of one light-day
articles.summary: NASA has announced that the Voyager 1 space probe will soon reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, having travelled at least 16 billion miles since its 1977 launch. Currently operating in interstellar space at approximately 36,000 miles per hour, the plutonium-powered craft continues to transmit daily scientific data alongside its twin, Voyager 2. Project manager Suzanne Dodd described the mission as a national treasure while noting ongoing communication efforts by a skeleton engineering team.
articles.description: The probe was launched in 1977, and it continues to relay space-related data back to a team of NASA scientists.

articles.headline: Stelco to recall 175 laid-off workers after Canadian government pressure
articles.title: Canada’s Stelco to recall 175 workers after government pressure
articles.summary: Canadian steelmaker Stelco has announced it will reinstate 175 laid-off workers at its Hamilton plant with retroactive pay following a dispute involving Industry Minister Melanie Joly and American owner Cleveland-Cliffs. The company stated that new customer agreements enabled finishing operations to restart on December 1. The layoffs had previously sparked friction over binding commitments made when Cleveland-Cliffs acquired Stelco in 2024, with officials citing market pressures and tariffs.
articles.description: Steelmaker promises back pay for workers whose layoffs its US owner blamed on tariffs, weak demand and imports.

articles.headline: US Democrats Schumer and Jeffries expected to retain congressional leadership roles
articles.title: Why US Democrats are expected to keep Schumer and Jeffries in power
articles.summary: Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer and House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries are widely expected to maintain their leadership positions as Democrats prepare to control both congressional chambers in January. Despite historic electoral gains, the prospect of continuity has sparked internal debate, with Senator Chris Van Hollen launching a formal challenge against Schumer. Critics argue the party requires new leadership to address shifting voter priorities, while supporters emphasize recent electoral successes and candidate recruitment.
articles.description: The prospect of keeping the Congressional leaders in power is exposing long-running tensions in the party.

articles.headline: Former civil servants urge Tamil Nadu chief minister to restore committee mandate
articles.title: Former civil servants urge CM Vijay to restore mandate of panel on Union-State relations
articles.summary: The Constitutional Conduct Group, comprising seventy-two former civil servants, has written an open letter urging Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to restore the original mandate of the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations. The signatories criticized the decision to transfer report preparation to the State Law Commission, warning it will cause delays and institutional knowledge loss.
articles.description: Responding to the State government’s contention that the committee was non-statutory in nature, the group pointed out that the State Law Commission was also an executive body

articles.headline: Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II visit escalates tensions between church factions
articles.title: Patriarch’s proposed visit to Manarcad church puts peace efforts on edge
articles.summary: The Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church warned that a potential visit by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II to the St. Mary's Jacobite Syrian Cathedral at Manarcad would aggravate ongoing factional disputes. Speaking on November 14, 2026, church representatives stated that visiting disputed properties violates court directives and undermines reconciliation efforts involving Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.
articles.description: Orthodox Church says it will welcome resolution of issues through discussions between the Patriarch and the Catholicos, but the Patriarch visiting disputed churches will only make matters worse

articles.headline: India air passenger traffic declines 2.9% in April-September period
articles.title: Air passenger traffic takes a hit, declines 2.9% in April-September
articles.summary: Air passenger traffic in India contracted 2.9 percent between April and September 2026, driven by a 7.1 percent drop in international travel and a 1.9 percent fall in domestic travel, according to The Hindu. The decline is linked to West Asian conflict disruptions, surging aviation turbine fuel costs, and soaring airfares that reached a 43 percent increase by October, prompting airlines to cut capacity.
articles.description: The decline in passenger traffic has been accompanied by a fall in aircraft movements, pointing to a reduction in the number of flights operated by airlines

articles.headline: Landslip in Idukki kills 59-year-old cardamom farmer
articles.title: Landslip in Idukki kills cardamom farmer
articles.summary: A 59-year-old cardamom farmer named Purayidathil Benny was killed on November 14, 2026, by a major landslip at Kadamakkuzhi near Kattappana in Idukki. Officials reported that despite two weeks of no rainfall, large-scale mining and explosive use on the opposite side of the hill triggered the disaster, prompting a detailed inspection report for the district collector.
articles.description: Almost eight acres of cardamom plantation destroyed in the incident at Kadamakkuzhi, near Kattappana. Preliminary findings point to large-scale quarrying and mining on the hill’s opposite side, using explosives, as the likely trigger.

articles.headline: Karnataka private transport associations urge cap on electric cab fleet
articles.title: Private transport associations urge Karnataka government to cap Vietnamese electric taxi aggregator’s fleet
articles.summary: The Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations asked Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to limit Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup's Green SM electric cab service to 100 vehicles in Bengaluru. The federation warned that corporate-backed low fares of around eight rupees per kilometer threaten the livelihoods of independent operators relying on bank loans for their vehicles.
articles.description: In a letter to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations sought immediate intervention to prevent what it described as unfair competition from the electric taxi fleet operated by Green SM

articles.headline: Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad warns Mission Samudra threatens fishing livelihoods
articles.title: KSSP warns Mission Samudra threatens livelihoods of traditional fishermen
articles.summary: The Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad urged the state government to reconsider Mission Samudra and the Maritime Board Amendment Bill, warning they could undermine traditional fishing livelihoods. General secretary V. Manoj Kumar and president C. Ramakrishnan stated the initiatives risk facilitating corporate control over coastal resources, eroding customary worker rights, and harming marine ecosystems across the state's marine fishing villages.
articles.description: Demands curbs on Maritime Board’s sweeping powers; calls for protection of coastal commons and fragile marine ecosystems

articles.headline: Karnataka organisations to launch year-long Constitution awareness campaign on November 26
articles.title: Year-long Constitution awareness campaign to begin on November 26
articles.summary: Dalit Sangharsha Samithigala Aikya Horata Chalana Samithi and Samvidhana Janandolana Samithi-Karnataka will launch a year-long awareness campaign titled Voice of Constitution, Voice of Public in Bengaluru. Former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah will inaugurate the initiative during Constitution Day celebrations. The programme aims to strengthen backward classes, minorities, and Dalits through study camps and discussions across all thirty-one districts of the state.

articles.headline: ED attaches properties worth ₹1.22 crore in KPSC recruitment scam
articles.title: KPSC ‘recruitment scam’: ED attaches properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to former chairman, member and IAS officer
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to former Karnataka Public Service Commission chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member Geetha B.V. Shivamurthy, and IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar. The action follows an investigation alleging the officials abused their positions in a veterinary officer recruitment scam involving question paper leaks and bribes.
articles.description: The three officials allegedly abused their official positions to collect illegal gratification from candidates in exchange for assured selection through question paper leaks, supply of candidate-specific answer keys and manipulation of confidential marks during the preparation of the 1:3 eligibility list

articles.headline: Spain and England meet in final UEFA Nations League group match
articles.title: Spain vs England: UEFA Nations League – predictions, how to watch, teams
articles.summary: England will face Spain in the UEFA Nations League Group A3 finale at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15. Spain holds a 15-point lead and a 43-match unbeaten streak, while England sits second with 12 points. Manager Thomas Tuchel aims to halt Spain's run, though both teams have already secured quarterfinal qualification for March following previous September fixtures.
articles.description: Spain, who are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive meetings, host England in Madrid on Sunday.

articles.headline: Bihar police identify over one lakh suspected cybercrime mule accounts
articles.title: Bihar Police identify over one lakh mule accounts across 38 districts
articles.summary: The Bihar Police Cyber Unit has identified 1,09,475 bank accounts across all 38 districts holding ₹72.53 crore in suspected cybercrime funds, according to Inspector General Ranjit Kumar Mishra. Patna recorded the highest number of mule accounts at 14,644. Authorities plan to target these accounts through the upcoming Cyber Prahar 5.0 campaign to tackle rising financial fraud.
articles.description: A total of 47,659 cybercrime complaints were registered in Bihar, while 5,69,160 complaints were registered at the national level during September and October.

articles.headline: Green turtles move from ‘endangered’ to ‘least concern’ status
articles.title: Green turtles move from ‘endangered’ to ‘least concern’ status
articles.description: Green turtles have been reclassified from endangered to ‘least concern’ in global conservation rankings.

articles.headline: Indian railways to launch weekly train between Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya
articles.title: Indian Railways to connect Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya through weekly train service
articles.summary: Indian Railways will operate a weekly train service connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya Cantt. in Uttar Pradesh, covering approximately 604 kilometres. According to the Ministry of Railways, the service aims to strengthen bilateral cultural ties by linking the two cities associated with the Ramayana tradition. The trains will run starting Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya.
articles.description: The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations

articles.headline: Himachal Pradesh approves financial assistance scheme for eligible women
articles.title: Himachal’s ₹1,500 allowance scheme: Who benefits and what’s the political impact? | Explained
articles.summary: The Himachal Pradesh government approved the Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna scheme during a cabinet meeting in Shimla chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Under the initiative, 3.50 lakh eligible women aged 18 to 59 will receive 1,500 rupees per month alongside 300 units of free electricity for beneficiary families across the state.
articles.description: What does the new Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna offer? Amid mounting debt concerns and Opposition criticism, will the government be able to ensure its smooth implementation?

articles.headline: India beat Bhutan 2-1 to reach SAFF Championship final
articles.title: India beat Bhutan 2-1 to enter SAFF Championship final
articles.summary: Defending champions India defeated Bhutan 2-1 on November 14, 2026, in Dhaka to enter the SAFF Championship final. P.V. Vishnu and Chinglensana Singh scored for India's under-23 reserve squad, while Tobden netted for Bhutan during a match that marked the historic debut of VAR in the tournament. India will face either Bangladesh or Pakistan in the November 17 final.
articles.description: The match marked the historic debut of the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system in the SAFF Championship
